subject.title: Feature request: fallback model chain for compaction and LCM summaryModel

question: Should OpenClaw add `agents.defaults.compaction.fallbacks` as a core public config surface now, and should Lossless `summaryModel` fallback live in the Lossless plugin or a generic context-engine SDK seam?
rationale: The remaining work adds provider/auth routing behavior and crosses the core compaction plus plugin-owned Lossless/context-engine boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent API shape.

options.title: Approve Embedded Core Fallback Plus Plugin-Owned Lossless
options.body: Add an explicit core fallback chain for embedded compaction and keep Lossless `summaryModel` fallback in the Lossless plugin unless a missing SDK seam is proven.

options.title: Design A Unified Context-Engine Contract
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers choose one API for embedded compaction, Lossless, and other context-engine summaries.

options.title: Keep Fallbacks Outside Core
options.body: Decline a new core config key and ask operators to use provider plugins, compaction providers, or external routing for summarizer fallback behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve Embedded Core Fallback Plus Plugin-Owned Lossless
recommendation.body: Add an explicit core fallback chain for embedded compaction and keep Lossless `summaryModel` fallback in the Lossless plugin unless a missing SDK seam is proven.

likelyOwner.reason: Their context-engine compaction delegate and compaction fallback history are the closest fit for deciding the core/plugin boundary.
